Lessons.Title: Interpreting & Using Function Notation
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning objective: interpret statements like f(a)>f(b), connect f(x) to ordered pairs (x,f(x)) and sketch a possible graph consistent with given values and inequalities. Independently authored Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 4 Lesson 3, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/4/3/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0). The source uses a drone's changing height, comparing point values and sketching function graphs.

Original first-party drone model (time t in seconds, height h in metres) is piecewise: h(t)=3t for 0≤t≤2; h(t)=6 for2<t≤5; h(t)=6−2(t−5) for5<t≤8. The drone rises to6 metres, remains constant, then descends to ground at t=8. Domain [0,8], range [0,6]. Each t has one height even when several times share height 6.

Interpret specific statements: h(0)=0, h(2)=6, h(4)=6, h(6)=4 and h(8)=0. So h(4)>h(6) and h(2)=h(4). The graph points are (0,0),(2,6),(4,6),(6,4),(8,0). A question asking whether h(t)>h(t+1) for all times is false because the drone initially climbs and later levels out.

Student task: describe values on three labeled time intervals, sketch the original piecewise function from statements, compare at least four input-output pairs, and explain what inequalities imply about the graph. Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 each for input/output interpretation, correct comparisons, coherent drawn graph and domain/time-interval reasoning.

KeyConcepts.Title: Ordered pair from function
KeyConcepts.Definition: An input x and its function value f(x) form plotted point (x,f(x)).

KeyConcepts.Title: Comparing outputs
KeyConcepts.Definition: f(a)>f(b) compares outputs at two separate inputs.
KeyConcepts.Rule: It does not compare a and b themselves.

KeyConcepts.Title: Intervals in graph descriptions
KeyConcepts.Definition: A function may rise, remain constant or fall over different input intervals.

WorkedExamples.Title: Evaluate two drone heights
WorkedExamples.Question: Compare h(4) and h(6) from the model.
WorkedExamples.Method: Represent the function with its stated input/output domain and verify the mathematical assertion.
Steps: At4 seconds drone is in constant interval, so h(4)=6 m.
At6 seconds descent rule gives6−2(6−5)=4 m.
WorkedExamples.Check: Both times fall in correctly selected segments.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find endpoint and range
WorkedExamples.Question: Find height at t=8 and the full range.
WorkedExamples.Method: Represent the function with its stated input/output domain and verify the mathematical assertion.
Steps: Descent rule at t=8 gives h(8)=6−2(8−5)=0.
Maximum height6 holds for t=2 through5.
Continuous segments cover every height between0 and6.
WorkedExamples.Check: Endpoints and intermediate heights all represented.

WorkedExamples.Title: Disprove a universal graph comparison
WorkedExamples.Question: Is h(t)>h(t+1) always true for 0≤t≤7?
WorkedExamples.Method: Represent the function with its stated input/output domain and verify the mathematical assertion.
Steps: One valid counterexample refutes the universal statement.
WorkedExamples.Answer: No; at t=0 the height rises.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Comparing arguments rather than function values
Applying one expression outside its piecewise interval
CommonMistakes.Correction: Check the time interval before evaluating.

SummaryPoints: Each point on a function graph is (input, output).
Output comparisons depend on function values, not argument ordering.
A piecewise graph can increase, remain constant and decrease while preserving uniqueness.
Graph and inequality interpretation require teacher review.
